item.title: US ranchers win pipeline compensation fight but face $300,000 legal bill, Supreme Court to hear case
item.description: A group of North Dakota ranchers who spent nearly $300,000 fighting a pipeline company over land compensation have taken their dispute over legal expenses to the US Supreme Court. Although they reached a settlement, an appeals court ruled that the company need not cover their legal costs. The Supreme Court will hear the case on November 9.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Stephen King’s $3 million pledge helped transform hometown library into a $9.6 million project
item.description: Stephen and Tabitha King have committed $3 million to the Bangor Public Library renovation, provided that $6 million is raised through community efforts. Thanks to local support and a municipal bond, the library hit its $9 million target, kickstarting essential upgrades like roof repairs and improved community spaces, honoring both its historical significance and modern audience requirements.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Forgotten John Constable Painting: $37 buy authenticated at $315,000; other 2024 finds hidden in plain sight
item.description: Hidden away in a cupboard for years, a painting believed to be by John Constable was recently found and has skyrocketed in value from its auction price of $37 to an astounding $315,000. This extraordinary revelation joins the ranks of remarkable discoveries, like a rare Lego mask and a Victorian brooch, which emphasize that ordinary objects can possess extraordinary worth.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Snakes Found Inside Airport: Venomous western browns spotted in terminal; experts explain heat-driven visits
item.description: As summer approaches, Alice Springs Airport is preparing for an influx of snake sightings, with multiple reports emerging from terminal areas. In response, the airport management has put in place monitoring systems and hired professionals for safe snake removal. Travelers are encouraged to remain alert and immediately report any sightings to airport personnel, emphasizing safety first in this reptilian season.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: In 2013, Tope Awotona emptied about $200,000 of his savings to build Calendly; eight years later investors valued the company at $3 billion
item.description: In 2013, Tope Awotona launched Calendly to tackle the difficulties professionals face in scheduling meetings. His journey began with personal funds, retirement savings, and loans, slowly gathering momentum. By 2021, Calendly had soared to a valuation exceeding $3 billion, driven by a booming user base and the demand for streamlined online scheduling.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: New York’s Plaza Hotel to close for four years to restore its historic facade
item.description: Starting in January 2027, New York City's iconic Plaza Hotel will embark on a significant facade restoration that is projected to last a minimum of four years. This closure will impact not only guests but also local residents. With previous renovations totaling $450 million between 2005 and 2008, and a pandemic-related shutdown in 2020, this restoration seeks to uphold the hotel's renowned architectural significance for generations to come.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: McClellan base closed in 2001; 25 years later, its 3,000-acre site boasts $600m in investment
item.description: Following its shutdown in 2001, McClellan Air Force Base prompted worries about economic decline. However, the area has been revitalized with McClellan Park, which boasts a $600 million investment and encompasses 10 million square feet of facilities. The site now functions as a public-use regional hub, enhancing local transportation and offering significant employment opportunities, while also emphasizing environmental restoration initiatives since the base's closure.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

California land trust sues to block roads across a 402-acre preserve saved from housing development
item.description: In a bid to protect the Clover Valley nature preserve, Placer Land Trust has initiated a lawsuit to block infrastructure development attempts. Established four years ago, this cherished area has faced housing pressures in the past. It comprises ancient oak forests, wetlands, and vital archaeological sites. The conservation easement was created to enforce permanent protection, and the legal proceedings will reinforce this against any existing development rights.

item.title: Edinburgh's historic Palm Houses reopen after a £23.5m restoration replaced 5,750 panes of glass
item.description: The Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh's Palm Houses have undergone extensive restorations costing £23.5 million over the past five years. Researchers carefully replaced all 5,750 glass panes to ensure they withstand harsh weather conditions. Following this work, nearly 600 rare plant specimens have been replanted in the glasshouses. The restoration enables continued conservation, education, and scientific discovery efforts related to endangered flora.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Texas courthouse vacant since 1977 faces demolition after $120 million repair estimates
item.description: In a decisive move, Nueces County officials have voted unanimously to proceed with the demolition of the aged 1914 courthouse, which has seen a decline over the decades and thwarted multiple redevelopment attempts. Expected to last around 130 days, the demolition aims to create opportunities for future development while eliminating continuous security expenses for taxpayers. While some historical artifacts will be saved, extensive asbestos contamination complicates the safe removal process.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Entrepreneur lists Aston Martin-designed home for $19.5m
item.description: Selling for $19.5 million, David Ingram's architecturally magnificent Hudson Valley home, designed by Aston Martin, is now available. The residence includes broad living spaces and striking details, reflecting five years of enhancements since he bought it in 2020. Noteworthy features include a swimming pool and an underground automotive gallery. Now focused on his wellness endeavors, Ingram rarely visits, prompting this sale of his exquisite property.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: Historic Ojai Tudor once home to composer Leo Robin sells for $4.6 million
item.description: Ojai's prestigious Estelle Clark Estate, emblematic of Tudor Revival architecture, has fetched $4.6 million after its initial listing at $6.495 million. This estate, built for the glamorous silent-film star Estelle Clark, also boasts a legacy linked to acclaimed composer Leo Robin. The appeal of historically rich and restored homes continues to thrive among buyers in the Ojai area.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: Indianapolis Dam Removal Project: City dismantles Emrichsville Dam; wildlife passage restored
item.description: The city of Indianapolis is set to dismantle the Emrichsville Dam as part of an initiative to revitalize the White River's natural flow. This endeavor is designed to improve aquatic habitats and ensure the safety of river goers. Funding has been obtained from a variety of federal and state organizations to assist with this project.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Submerged Archaeological Sites Study: Researchers map two underwater Aboriginal sites; stone moved 23 km
item.description: Archaeologists collaborated with Indigenous rangers to explore submerged sites off Murujuga in Western Australia. They uncovered artefacts and evidence of past human activity before rising sea levels altered the landscape. Two key locations highlighted interactions with freshwater resources and elevated terrains. The research involved several universities and emphasized the importance of Indigenous expertise in cultural heritage.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk
